public_rationale: The records are consistent with caution about practical readiness, but do not settle the full assertion. SayCan demonstrated useful kitchen-task planning, and Code as Policies demonstrated LLM-generated robot control. Neither establishes safe general household operation. Gato was described as a research prototype without user deployment, but that does not establish that every October option was inadequate. Conversely, missing safety demonstrations do not prove that AlphaStar and all contemporary LLM systems would surely be unsafe. The available evidence therefore supports neither a decisive endorsement nor a contradiction under the stated household-controller reading.
limitations: The selected experiments predate the target snapshot and are context rather than outcome evidence.
Task success, practical adequacy, and physical safety are different measures.
Some AlphaStar primary material could not be retrieved in a usable form.
A narrower claim that no safe general household controller had been demonstrated would require less evidence than the categorical wording assessed here.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is currently no viable general intelligence to install in a domestic humanoid robot; LLMs and AlphaStar would be unsafe and inadequate.
conditions: as general intelligence for a domestic humanoid robot

statement.excerpt: The answer is that at present we have no viable option; AlphaStar and LLMs would surely be unsafe and inadequate; and we don’t yet have anything markedly better.
statement.document_title: Three baffling claims about AI and machine learning in four days, statistical errors in top journals, and claims from Yann LeCun that you should not believe.

from_speaker: AlphaStar and LLMs would surely be unsafe and inadequate
we don’t yet have anything markedly better
a safe and useful domestic humanoid robot
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that available AI could not provide sufficiently reliable and safe general household decision-making for a domestic humanoid robot.
The surrounding hypothetical grants successful motor control. Failures of locomotion or manipulation hardware alone therefore cannot establish the claim.
Viability means practical suitability across ordinary household tasks and unexpected situations. It does not require perfect performance or a particular philosophical definition of intelligence.
The target is the publicly observable state on 2022-10-16. This technology has no regular reporting period, so I use the post-date snapshot rather than inventing a quarterly or annual window.
Earlier experiments inform that snapshot but remain context when their measured events occurred outside the target period.
The household application defines the scope of this observation; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishing that the available candidate controllers lacked the reliability, general household competence, and safety needed for this use, including evidence supporting the asserted inadequacy and unsafety of AlphaStar and contemporary LLM systems. Missing demonstrations alone are insufficient to establish the entire claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented system available at the target date that could provide safe, adequate general household decision-making with functioning motor skills would contradict the no-option assertion. Successful isolated tasks alone would not suffice.

evidence.explanation: The dated update reports 84% planning success and 74% execution success; the results describe 101 tasks in two kitchen settings. This establishes useful LLM-based household-task capabilities, but neither general household safety nor failure after granting perfect motor control.

The original preprint describes LLM-generated control policies demonstrated across robot platforms. This challenges a reading that LLMs had no useful control capabilities, but does not establish safe general operation of a domestic humanoid.

evidence.explanation: The paper describes a generalist research agent, calls the work proof-of-concept, and reports no user deployment. This is consistent with limited practical readiness, but its May status does not establish the absence of every viable option in October.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated evaluations of systems available on 2022-10-16 showing safe, reliable general household decision-making would contradict the no-option assertion. A sufficiently comprehensive historical assessment documenting capability and safety failures across the available candidates, with motor limitations separated out, could support it.
